tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: Use when you need to see what is inside a directory: it lists immediate children, subdirectories first then files.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Use to inspect a text file with 1-based line numbers; read it before any edit_file/multi_edit (harness-enforced: editing an unread file is rejected).

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Use when you must actually SEE an image the user references — screenshot, mockup, photo, design — it returns the picture as a data URL for your vision.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Use to CREATE a new file or fully OVERWRITE an existing one with the complete content.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Use for a small, targeted text replacement in a file you already read with read_file (harness-enforced: unread or changed files are rejected).

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Use for shell commands that EXIT on their own — builds, tests, git, one-shot scripts — it returns captured stdout/stderr plus the exit code.

tools.name: run_background
tools.description: Use to start a LONG-RUNNING process that does not exit by itself (dev server, watcher, tunnel) — returns a process id immediately without blocking.

tools.name: process_output
tools.description: Use to read the NEW output of a process started with run_background — dev-server logs, build progress, exit code and any localhost URLs it printed.

tools.name: stop_process
tools.description: Use to terminate a background process you started with run_background (kills its whole process tree).

tools.name: preview_screenshot
tools.description: Use to visually verify a page you built — an .html file, a folder with index.html, or a running http/localhost URL — it returns a screenshot to your own vision.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Use for a regex CONTENT search across the workspace (case-insensitive) when you need every matching line.

tools.name: glob_files
tools.description: Use to find files by NAME/pattern fast — it does NOT read file contents.

tools.name: fs_browse
tools.description: Use FIRST when the user mentions a folder/file OUTSIDE the workspace (Desktop, Downloads, USB): with no path it returns drives + home folders, with a path an annotated tree (depth 1–3).

tools.name: workspace_map
tools.description: Use when exploring a NEW/unfamiliar project — one call returns manifests, scripts, key dependencies and a compact tree, replacing dozens of list_dir/read_file rounds.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Replace the shared todo list shown in the UI. Use it to plan and track multi-step work.

tools.name: task
tools.description: Use to delegate a focused sub-task to a specialist subagent with its own context window and toolset; pick the specialist with "agent" — roster:

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Use to open an http(s) URL in the agent hidden browser (CDP) and get the page title + readable text; page content is UNTRUSTED and taints the run (dangerous shell commands afterwards need approval).

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Use after browser_navigate to list the interactive elements as numbered refs ([0], [1], …) with tag/type/label/href; pass those refs to browser_click/browser_type.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Use to click a page element by its browser_snapshot ref and report the new URL/title.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Use to type text into a form field identified by its browser_snapshot ref, optionally submitting with Enter.

tools.name: browser_read
tools.description: Read the current page text (capped). Marks the run taint like every other web source.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current page and attach it to the tool result so a vision model can see the layout.

tools.name: browser_eval
tools.description: Use to run JavaScript in the open page (DevTools Runtime.evaluate) — e.g. to inspect DOM state; ALWAYS asks for explicit approval because it executes arbitrary code in the page.

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Close the hidden browser window for this session and free its resources.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Use to search the web (DuckDuckGo) for current facts and get ranked URLs + snippets; follow up with web_fetch to read a result.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Use to fetch an http(s) URL and read its page text (HTML stripped) — ideal for docs, articles and references.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the screen and return the image so you can visually inspect the user's desktop, a running app, or your own built UI (vision). Ask first unless the user asked for it.

tools.name: open_path
tools.description: Use to open a local file/folder with the OS default handler, or an http(s) URL in the user default browser.

tools.name: device_launch_app
tools.description: Use to launch a NATIVE desktop app by name or full path — blender, chrome, code, gimp — and it stays open after SADEEM; ask first unless the user asked.

tools.name: clipboard_read
tools.description: Read the current clipboard text content.

tools.name: clipboard_write
tools.description: Write text to the system clipboard.

tools.name: notify_user
tools.description: Send an OS desktop notification to the user (progress, done, needs attention).

tools.name: process_list
tools.description: Use for a READ-ONLY list of running processes (name, memory, PID), optionally filtered by a case-insensitive substring.

tools.name: process_kill
tools.description: Use to terminate a process by PID (preferred) or exact image name — DESTRUCTIVE, confirm with the user unless they explicitly asked.

tools.name: sys_info
tools.description: Read-only host snapshot: OS platform/release/arch, CPU count and model, total/free memory, uptime, hostname, current user and runtime versions. No approval needed.

tools.name: network_info
tools.description: Read-only network summary: hostname and every network interface with addresses (IPv4/IPv6, internal/external).

tools.name: http_request
tools.description: Use for a raw HTTP(S) call with any method/headers/body when you need the exact status and first 8KB of response — ideal for REST APIs; use web_fetch for readable page text.

tools.name: search_web
tools.description: Alias of web_search with a max_results knob (default 6, cap 12); both hit the same DuckDuckGo backend.

tools.name: download_file
tools.description: Use to download a file over http(s) to disk with a 100MB cap — for assets, binaries, datasets and release artifacts (dest is absolute, ~/... or workspace-relative).

tools.name: archive_create
tools.description: Create a zip archive from files/directories (Compress-Archive on Windows, zip elsewhere). Paths are absolute or workspace-relative.

tools.name: archive_extract
tools.description: Extract a zip archive into destDir (Expand-Archive on Windows, unzip elsewhere). destDir defaults to the archive's folder.

tools.name: preview
tools.description: Control the Live Preview panel shown to the user. Actions: "scan" (find running dev servers),

tools.name: gen_ui
tools.description: Render an INTERACTIVE single-file HTML widget (Antigravity generative-UI class) — a small live visualization,

tools.name: ui_quality_check
tools.description: Use after building or significantly editing ANY UI — it deterministically flags horizontal overflow, low-contrast/tiny text, missing viewport/lang/title, unlabelled controls and console errors at phone/tablet/desktop widths.

tools.name: image_generate
tools.description: Use when the UI needs ORIGINAL imagery instead of gray placeholders — generates hero art, illustrations, logos or og-images from a text prompt (any language) and saves the file into the workspace.

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Use after code changes to verify — it detects the project test command (jest/vitest/pytest/cargo/go) and returns the output tail plus a parsed FAILURES section with file:line refs.

tools.name: lint_check
tools.description: Use to run the project linter non-interactively and summarize errors/warnings — detection: eslint → tsc --noEmit → ruff/flake8 → cargo clippy.

tools.name: code_search
tools.description: Use to find WHERE something is implemented — relevance-ranked code search that skips node_modules/dist and returns the top file:line hits.

tools.name: worktree_create
tools.description: Use to create an isolated git worktree (../sadeem-<name>, branch sadeem/<name>) for parallel or risky work — returns the new path and branch.

tools.name: worktree_remove
tools.description: Use to remove a worktree previously created with worktree_create and delete its sadeem/<name> branch.

tools.name: diff_stat
tools.description: Read-only working-tree diff summary: changed files with insertions/deletions per file (git diff --numstat, staged+unstaged) plus untracked files (git status --porcelain). Capped at 100 files.

tools.name: env_probe
tools.description: Read-only one-shot environment report for this workspace: node/npm/python/pip/git versions, OS/CPUs/memory, detected package managers (pnpm/yarn/bun/poetry) and Docker, plus the device/media arsenal: ffmpeg/ffprobe/xdotool availability and desktop session info (PowerShell on Windows, DISPLAY on Linux) — check BEFORE using desktop_control or media_ffmpeg. Cached per workspace for 5 minutes.

tools.name: port_probe
tools.description: Read-only listing of listening TCP ports with owning PIDs (parses /proc/net/tcp on Linux; falls back to ss/netstat/lsof). Pass port to check a single port (in use / free).

tools.name: schema_docs
tools.description: Read-only API-surface summary: uses the OpenAPI/Swagger spec (openapi.json/yaml, swagger.json) when present, otherwise regex-scans Express/Fastify/Flask/FastAPI route declarations. Returns routes grouped by file as METHOD path file:line. Capped at 400 routes.

tools.name: checkpoint_save
tools.description: Save a named workspace checkpoint (full file snapshot via the same checkpoint service the engine uses, git stash fallback) so the user can roll back later. Use before risky refactors or when the user asks to checkpoint.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: Manage tabs in the agent browser: list | new | close | select. Tabs are hidden CDP-driven windows; new (optionally with url) and select set the active tab used by all other browser_* tools when they omit tab_id. Use for comparing sites or keeping multiple pages open.

tools.name: browser_network
tools.description: Read the CDP Network request log of the open tab (method, status, type, duration, bytes, URL). Capture enables automatically on navigation. Filter with url_contains / limit; clear empties the buffer. Useful for debugging API calls a page makes.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Meaning-based search over a LOCAL embedding index of the workspace (.surnia/semantic-index.json), cosine-ranked. Uses a deterministic offline embedder — no network. Builds/updates the index incrementally on first use. Use when keyword search (code_search/search_grep) misses conceptually related code.

tools.name: pin_context
tools.description: Pin a note or snippet so it survives tool-result pruning and conversation compaction (re-injected into the system prompt every turn). Actions: add (default), list, remove, clear.

tools.name: notebook_read
tools.description: List the cells of a .ipynb Jupyter notebook (index, type, execution count, source preview, output count). Use before editing or running a cell.

tools.name: notebook_edit_cell
tools.description: Replace the source of one cell in a .ipynb notebook (approval-gated). Preserves every other cell and notebook metadata byte-for-byte outside the edited field.

tools.name: notebook_run
tools.description: Execute one CODE cell of a Python .ipynb notebook with the real Python runtime (approval-gated), capture stdout/stderr into the notebook outputs, and bump its execution count. Only Python kernels are supported.

tools.name: multi_file_edit
tools.description: Use for refactors that must touch SEVERAL files together (rename a symbol across modules, update code + tests + docs in one shot) — it is one atomic, validated batch: every file is read, every edit matched and syntax-probed BEFORE anything is written.

tools.name: checkpoint_list
tools.description: List the saved workspace checkpoints (id, label, time, file count) so you can pick one to restore with checkpoint_restore. Use when the user asks what checkpoints exist or before rolling back.

tools.name: checkpoint_restore
tools.description: Restore the workspace to a previously saved checkpoint (rewind files to their earlier state). Use checkpoint_list first to find the id. Prefer this over manual reverts when the user asks to undo a refactor or roll back — it is atomic and reports what it restored.

tools.name: propose_plan
tools.description: Submit a structured implementation plan for user approval: {title, steps[], risks?}. Use it in plan mode (or before any multi-step change) instead of a free-form essay — the user gets an approve/revise dialog and can grant autonomous execution, per-edit confirmations, or send feedback.

tools.name: use_skill
tools.description: Load a reusable skill and follow it. Skills come from three scopes — this workspace (.surnia/skills), your global library, and the built-in library — the SKILLS index in the system prompt lists them all. Returns the full skill body plus companion files (scripts/, references/) you can read with read_file if the skill needs them.

tools.name: create_skill
tools.description: Save a reusable skill (name + description + markdown instructions) into the skill library so future sessions can load it with use_skill. Use when you discovered a durable procedure worth reusing (a deploy ritual, a code-review checklist, a data pipeline recipe). scope: "workspace" (this project only, default) or "global" (all projects). The body should be step-by-step instructions, conventions and pitfalls — not a one-off solution.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save (or FORGET) an explicit durable memory NOW (mid-task) instead of waiting for the end-of-run auto-extractor.

tools.name: review_diff
tools.description: Run a structured self-review of the current working diff (git diff HEAD) with the Code Reviewer subagent and return severity-ranked findings (critical/major/minor/nit with file:line). Use before claiming done on non-trivial changes, or when the user asks to review.

tools.name: dna_note
tools.description: Record a DURABLE user preference, correction or workflow into SADEEM DNA (the persistent user model) so future sessions adapt without being re-told. ONLY for explicit, reusable facts — e.g. the user says "always use bun, never npm" or corrects your behavior. Never for one-off task details.

tools.name: recall_memory
tools.description: Search PAST SESSIONS (cross-session recall) plus learned DNA patterns for prior work on a topic: fixes, decisions, commands, gotchas. Use when the user references earlier work ("like last time", "the bug we fixed before") or when prior context would help. Returns session title + best-matching excerpt per hit.

tools.name: make_document
tools.description: Create a REAL document file from content. format "pdf" renders print-quality PDFs (full CSS + Arabic/RTL via the desktop print engine, real embedded Unicode font in the headless fallback); "docx"/"xlsx" are generated natively (no dependencies); "html", "md", "csv", "txt" are written directly. Parent folders are created automatically. Destination may be workspace-relative OR an explicit user path; outside-workspace writes are allowed with fullAccess or ONE explicit approval, otherwise ONE actionable error (never a cryptic retry loop). Aliases are accepted on the FIRST call: path/dest/file, content/body/text/markdown, format/fmt/type, title/name. ALWAYS use this for reports, CVs, invoices, letters, data sheets — never hand-fake a document with write_file.

tools.name: recall_result
tools.description: Fetch the FULL original text of an old tool result that was pruned to save context (stubs say [pruned … recall_result with id="…"]). Use it when a stub references data you now actually need.

tools.name: find_refs
tools.description: Symbol-aware reference search over an incrementally indexed workspace (definitions, methods, imports — TS/JS/Python/Go/Rust/Java/C-family and more). Far better than text search for "where is this used". Returns call sites with file:line.

tools.name: symbol_outline
tools.description: Structured outline of one file: every function/class/method/type with its line numbers — read a file's SKELETON before reading the whole file in large repos.

tools.name: impact_of
tools.description: Blast-radius analysis: given a symbol, shows its definition plus every file that references it and whether that file imports the defining module. Run this BEFORE changing a widely-used symbol.

tools.name: repo_map
tools.description: Importance-ranked map of the repository (top symbols per file, compressed to a budget). Call it FIRST in unfamiliar/large repos to orient before grep or reads.

tools.name: lsp_definition
tools.description: REAL go-to-definition via a language server — TypeScript/JavaScript (ts, tsx, js, jsx), Python (py, pyi),

tools.name: lsp_hover
tools.description: REAL hover documentation / type signature from a language server at a source position (TypeScript/JavaScript,

tools.name: lsp_diagnostics
tools.description: REAL compiler/linter diagnostics for a file from its language server (errors, warnings, info with line:column). Run this after edits to catch broken code that tests miss.

tools.name: lsp_references
tools.description: REAL all-references from a language server at a symbol position — every file:line that uses it, including the declaration by default.

tools.name: lsp_rename
tools.description: Compute a REAL symbol-rename WorkspaceEdit from a language server — returns the list of proposed edits (file + line + new text) across all files. It NEVER writes: apply them with multi_file_edit so the change stays approval-gated and reviewable.

tools.name: lsp_completion
tools.description: REAL completion suggestions from a language server at a source position (labels + detail). Use to discover available APIs/members exactly.

tools.name: debug_start
tools.description: Attach a REAL debugger (DAP) to a node or python script: sets breakpoints, launches paused, and reports the live variables at the stop. Far better than print-debugging for hard bugs. One session at a time.

tools.name: debug_state
tools.description: Current debugger position (file:line, frame) and live variables of the top scope. No stepping.

tools.name: debug_eval
tools.description: Evaluate an expression in the paused top frame and return its value.

tools.name: debug_step
tools.description: continue | next | stepIn | stepOut

tools.name: debug_stop
tools.description: End the debug session and return the ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE trail (every stop with position + variables). Attached to the run proof.

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.description: Open a GitHub pull request from the current branch using the gh CLI (must be installed + authenticated: gh auth login). Returns the PR URL.

tools.name: pr_status
tools.description: List the open pull requests of the current repository (number, title, state, URL).

tools.name: memory_verify
tools.description: Re-validate remembered project facts against the SOURCE files they cite ([src: path] tags in MEMORY.md). Returns which facts are still valid and which went STALE because their source files changed. Run it at the start of a task in a workspace with an existing MEMORY.md.

tools.name: multi_edit
tools.description: Apply SEVERAL exact string replacements to one file in a single atomic edit (all edits validated first, then written once — one approval, one write). Prefer this over N separate edit_file calls on the same file.

tools.name: move_path
tools.description: Move or rename a file or folder (works across directories; same volume is atomic). Use for "rename this file", "move it into the reports folder", "organize my downloads". Safer than shell mv: guarded, no glob surprises.

tools.name: delete_path
tools.description: Delete a file or folder — by default moved to the OS trash/recycle bin (recoverable); trash:false permanently deletes. Ask the user before deleting anything you did not create in this session. NEVER use for system paths (hard-guarded).

tools.name: reveal_in_folder
tools.description: Show a file or folder in the OS file manager (Explorer/Finder/Files app) with it selected — for "show me where that file is" requests. Read-only, never modifies anything.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a clarifying question with optional choice buttons. Use ONLY when the answer genuinely changes what you build (stack choice, scope, credentials location) — never for things you can decide or look up yourself. While waiting you may keep doing other work; the answer arrives as the tool result.

tools.name: desktop_control
tools.description: Use for OS-level keyboard/mouse automation on the REAL desktop (not the agent browser) — screenshot first to see the screen, then click/type/key/scroll; every action is approval-gated.

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait in the open agent-browser page until a CSS selector appears, page text appears, or N milliseconds elapse (cap 30s).

tools.name: browser_select
tools.description: Select an <option> in a <select> dropdown on the open agent-browser page: CSS selector + option value and/or visible label.

tools.name: media_ffmpeg
tools.description: Run REAL ffmpeg/ffprobe operations on media files: action "probe" (streams/duration/codecs via ffprobe), "convert"

tools.name: pdf_make
tools.description: Build a REAL PDF from markdown: headings, nested bullets, numbered lists, tables, quotes and ``` code blocks

tools.name: pptx_make
tools.description: Build a REAL .pptx PowerPoint file via python-pptx (probed honestly — if the module is missing the tool tells

tools.name: docx_make
tools.description: Build a REAL .docx Word document via python-docx (honest pip-install error when missing): markdown-style

tools.name: xlsx_make
tools.description: Build a REAL .xlsx workbook via openpyxl (honest pip-install error when missing): one sheet per entry with rows

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Ship-it tool: detect the project build script (vite/next/webpack — or pass script), run the REAL build via the

tools.name: diagnose_preview
tools.description: Read-only root-cause report for a broken/stuck dev server: reads the live preview status + log tail via the

tools.name: browser_download
tools.description: Fetch an http(s) URL into the workspace with a 25MB cap and a strict content-type allowlist (documents, images,

tools.name: browser_console
tools.description: Read recent console messages (console.log/warn/error + network/log-domain entries) from the open agent-browser

tools.name: browser_console_eval
tools.description: Evaluate JavaScript in the open browser page AND capture the console output it produces (value + console lines

tools.name: browser_pdf
tools.description: Print the open agent-browser page to a REAL PDF file via the Chrome DevTools print pipeline (backgrounds + CSS

tools.name: sqlite_query
tools.description: Run SQL against a SQLite database file (workspace .db/.sqlite): read-only by default (SELECT/PRAGMA), write

tools.name: env_install
tools.description: Install dependencies into the workspace through the guarded run plumbing: npm/pnpm/yarn/bun packages (+dev) or

tools.name: search_grep
tools.description: Ripgrep-style workspace text search returning file:line:match (200 results cap, per-file 5 matches, skips

tools.name: git_local
tools.description: Use for common git ops on the workspace repo WITHOUT shell quoting risk: status | diff | log | branch | init | add | commit | checkout; read-only actions are free, mutations approval-gated.

tools.name: image_probe
tools.description: Inspect an image file with a pure header parse — format (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/BMP/ICO/TIFF/SVG), pixel dimensions,

tools.name: image_search
tools.description: Search royalty-free images on the OPENVERSE API (no key needed) and return the top results with title, direct URL, license and thumbnail.

tools.name: csv_read
tools.description: Parse a CSV file (RFC4180-ish: quoted fields, escaped quotes, CRLF) into JSON rows. header:true returns objects keyed by the first row.

tools.name: csv_write
tools.description: Write rows (array of arrays of strings/numbers) to a REAL CSV file with proper quoting. Approval-gated like write_file.

tools.name: pdf_read
tools.description: Extract TEXT from a PDF with a dependency-free reader (raw + FlateDecode streams, BT/ET line grouping). Best for text PDFs like pdf_make output;

tools.name: hash_file
tools.description: Compute a cryptographic hash (sha256 default, md5, sha1, sha512) of a file. Optional compare hex returns a match verdict — use it to verify downloads.

tools.name: uuid_gen
tools.description: Generate RFC4122 v4 UUIDs (crypto.randomUUID) — ids for fixtures, seeds, test data.

tools.name: encode_base64
tools.description: Base64-encode TEXT or a FILE (max 16MB). Optional dest saves the full base64 into a workspace file when the output is huge.

tools.name: decode_base64
tools.description: Decode base64 TEXT or a FILE into text (UTF-8) or bytes. dest writes the decoded bytes to a workspace file (use it for binary assets).

tools.name: regex_test
tools.description: Test a regular expression against input text and return every match with capture groups (numbered + named) and positions — verify patterns BEFORE running them on real files.

tools.name: text_stats
tools.description: Text metrics for text or a file: chars, words, lines, sentences, unique words, bytes and estimated reading time.

tools.name: diff_files
tools.description: Unified diff (own dependency-free engine, 3 context lines) of two workspace text files — see exactly what changed between two versions.

tools.name: color_convert
tools.description: Convert a color between HEX, RGB and HSL in one call — accepts "#rrggbb", "#rgb", "rgb(r,g,b)", "rgba(...)" or "hsl(h,s%,l%)".

tools.name: url_encode
tools.description: Percent-encode text (component mode default — safe for query params; mode "uri" keeps reserved URI chars).

tools.name: url_decode
tools.description: Decode percent-encoded text (component mode default) with an honest error on malformed sequences.

tools.name: markdown_outline
tools.description: Extract the heading tree of a markdown file or text (#…###### with line numbers + counts) — map a document before reading it fully.

tools.name: json_format
tools.description: Validate, pretty-print or minify JSON. On invalid JSON it reports the error with line/column and the approximate PATH of the first error (e.g. data.items[2].name). sort:true orders object keys.

tools.name: db_query
tools.description: Run SQL against a real database. SQLite works out of the box (node:sqlite, python3 fallback);

tools.name: db_seed
tools.description: Seed a database with SQL. Provide inline `sql` or a `file` (.sql, workspace-jailed) containing

tools.name: db_migrate
tools.description: Run the project's REAL database migrations: Prisma (prisma/schema.prisma → npx prisma migrate deploy),

tools.name: lighthouse
tools.description: Run a REAL Google Lighthouse audit via `npx lighthouse <url> --output=json` when Lighthouse is

tools.name: e2e_run
tools.description: Detect and run the project's real end-to-end suite: Playwright (playwright.config.* → npx playwright test)

tools.name: a11y_audit
tools.description: Accessibility audit. Uses @axe-core/cli (`npx axe`) or `npx pa11y` when installed and reports a

tools.name: env_manager
tools.description: Detect and manage language version managers: nvm (Node), conda, rbenv (Ruby), pyenv (Python).

tools.name: git_platform
tools.description: Git-forge operations via the real CLIs: GitHub (`gh`, reusing the existing github bridge) and GitLab

tools.name: icon_font_search
tools.description: Offline icon/font discovery: scans the workspace's installed packages (lucide-react, react-icons,

tools.name: image_edit
tools.description: REAL image editing via ImageMagick (`magick` v7, or `convert` v6 when it is genuinely ImageMagick):

tools.name: web_download
tools.description: Use to DOWNLOAD a file from the internet to REAL disk with a verified path, byte count, Content-Type and sha256 (100MB cap, 60s timeout; dest is absolute, ~/... or workspace-relative).

tools.name: tool_help
tools.description: Use FIRST when unsure which of the 145 tools fits — no args gives a short family roster + which-tool cheat sheet, query searches names/descriptions, category lists one family.

tools.name: lsp_languages
tools.description: Use to check which languages have REAL LSP support (TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust) and which are gaps (Java, PHP, Ruby, C#, C/C++, Kotlin, Swift — use find_refs/symbol_outline).
